Service

Responsive experiences that shine on every device.

Mobile and responsive web design done with the same rigor I bring to enterprise products: real user research, performance-aware decisions, and component-ready handoff that engineering can actually build.

Mobile

First approach

iOS

and Android

All

Breakpoints covered

Deliverables

What I bring to mobile and web projects.

Responsive web design

Pixel-precise layouts that work across breakpoints — not just desktop shrunk to mobile, but experiences designed from the smallest screen up.

Mobile app UX/UI

Native iOS and Android patterns applied with intention. Platform conventions respected where they serve the user; broken where they would limit the experience.

Cross-device user flows

Mapping how users move between devices across a session — starting on phone, completing on desktop — and designing the handoff moments that make multi-device use seamless.

Touch interaction design

Gesture patterns, touch targets, and interaction models designed for the constraints and capabilities of touch input: thumbs, gloves, one-handed use.

Performance-aware design

Design decisions that account for real-world network conditions, device memory constraints, and the performance budget engineering works within.

Component-ready specs

Design files structured for component-based development: named layers, consistent spacing tokens, interaction annotations, and dev-ready handoff.

Approach

Mobile-first is a constraint, not a checkbox.

Starting from the smallest screen forces good information hierarchy decisions. If it works at 375px, it will work everywhere. If you have to hide content on mobile, you probably have too much of it.

I design for the real conditions in which mobile products are used: outdoors in bright light, on a crowded train with one hand occupied, with slow network connections, with notifications interrupting the flow. Constraints that reveal which design decisions actually hold up.

Accessibility first

Touch targets, color contrast, and screen reader support are not afterthoughts — they are the starting conditions for every mobile design I build.

Real device testing

Designs are reviewed on physical devices, not just browser simulators. The difference matters more than most teams realize.

Platform conventions matter

iOS and Android users have different expectations. I apply platform patterns where they serve the user and diverge deliberately when the experience requires it.
